day1_insight: Recent rain (~5 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; and daytime high temperature is lowering risk — warmer conditions can help bacteria survive longer (and track the season). The most recent sample, 6 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL.
